tutorials.title: Give an Agent the Trigger, Never the Authority
Paper Trade First, Then Draw the Authority Map
tutorials.subtitle: Test an agentic DeFi workflow without a wallet, then turn it into a human-reviewed OpenZaps authority map

hero.alt: OpenZaps Virtual Trading banner reading "Trade the route. Risk nothing." beside a wallet-free paper-trading safety checklist.

claims.text: Virtual Trading is a browser-local paper-trading surface with virtual funds and no wallet, approval, signature, or transaction.
Request a Zap provides a human-reviewed authority map and is not an automatic deployment promise.
An agent may submit a due run but cannot widen the signed recipient, amount, cadence, floor, adapter, asset, or calldata.
OpenZaps has not completed an external audit.

tutorials.title: Earn the Pool's Fees, Not an Emission
tutorials.subtitle: How a Clanker v4 fee position becomes 100 tokenized shares, why 50 of them fund a seven-day 0xZAPS staking campaign, and the exact reads to run before you stake

hero.alt: The OpenZaps fee rewards page reading "Stake 0xZAPS. Claim WETH from the pool's trading fees." beside a campaign terms panel showing the seven-day window and claim deadline.

claims.text: The campaign stakes 0xZAPS and pays rewards only in WETH, which is bridged ether and is not minted by the campaign, the vault, or OpenZaps.
The reward source is the Clanker v4 hook fee paid by swaps in the 0xZAPS/aeWETH pool; the pool is dynamic-fee and the hook owner can change the rate.
A vault minted a fixed supply of 100 fee shares and 50 of them were transferred into the campaign contract before launch.
Holding 0xZAPS grants no fee rights; a claim accrues only while tokens are staked in the campaign contract.
Rewards are split by time-weighted stake across a fixed seven-day window and expire at the claim deadline.
Harvest and reward synchronization are permissionless, so no operator can withhold rewards and none is obligated to advance them.
No yield, rate, or APR is promised; rewards depend entirely on trading volume that no participant controls.
OpenZaps has not completed an external audit, and the campaign and vault contracts are not source-verified on the public explorer.
